svg.aria-label: The cytology and haematology smear as a detection primitive. Left: one glass slide holds tens of thousands to millions of cells in a mostly single layer, with overlapping clusters that are three-dimensional, so scanners capture several focal planes. Typical targets: a cervical liquid-based slide needs at least 5,000 squamous cells for adequacy and the abnormal cells may be a handful; a blood-smear differential counts 100 to 200 white cells among millions of red cells; a thick malaria smear counts parasites against 200 white cells, and ring-stage parasites are a few tens of pixels wide. Right: four stacked output layers read from the same slide: cell instances, cell class, slide-level grade such as Bethesda or Paris category, and a patient decision such as refer, repeat or treat.
svg.title: The smear: one slide, many cells, four output layers
svg.text: The smear: a few diagnostic cells hidden among 10⁴–10⁶ ordinary ones
Approximate, typical values. Counts vary by preparation (conventional vs liquid-based), stain and scanner.

g.text: Mostly a monolayer…
…plus 3-D clusters, so scanners
take several focal planes (z-stack)
target = one abnormal cell
Cervical / urine cytology (Pap, LBC, urine)
≥ 5,000 squamous cells for LBC adequacy; 10⁴–10⁵ on a slide
positives may be a handful of cells (ASC-US … HSIL, HGUC)
readout: Bethesda / Paris category per slide
Peripheral blood / bone marrow smear
differential = 100–200 white cells among millions of red cells
13+ fine-grained classes; blasts and rare cells are the long tail
readout: cell counts → leukaemia / AML subtype flag
Malaria thin / thick smear
thick film: parasites counted against 200 white cells (WHO)
ring-stage P. falciparum ≈ a few tens of pixels wide
species (4) + stage; field images from phones / cheap scopes
readout: positive?, species, parasitaemia

svg.text: Four output layers on the same slide

g.text: 1 · Cell instances
boxes / masks in dense, touching, overlapping cells
metric: mAP@50, recall of tiny objects, count correlation
2 · Cell class
WBC type, parasite species/stage, atypia grade
metric: macro-F1 (long tail), calibration under shift
3 · Slide grade
MIL / top-k aggregation over 10⁴+ cells
metric: slide AUC; sensitivity at a fixed specificity
4 · Patient decision
refer / repeat / treat; triage of what a human reads
metric: reader-study sensitivity, review time, NPV

svg.text: Layer 1 is mostly solved on clean data;
2025–26 progress is in layers 2–4 and in robustness to slide shift.
